transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-01 15:00 PDT | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (CTO, Liminal Tech), Jenna Ross (Lead ML Engineer), Marcus Lee (DevOps)

[00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ava from Redwood, AE on this account. Diego our SE is here too. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Samir Patel: Good, thanks. Excited to learn more, short on time so we'll try to be concise.
[00:11] Ava Chen: Totally. Agenda: quick intros, understand your use case & constraints, walk through our PLG quickstart and credits, and talk about next steps.
[00:20] Jenna Ross: Sounds good. I'll give a quick background — we build Liminal's document summarization pipeline, real-time customer support summarization. Currently using an open model host but struggling with cost spikes and latency. We're evaluating Redwood for hosted API and to see if Dedicated makes sense.
[00:36] Diego Morales: Helpful, thanks. When you say latency, what's your p95 target and typical request size?
[00:42] Jenna Ross: We're aiming for p95 < 300ms for 512-token sequences in production; dev can be looser. Throughput is modest — a few hundred requests per minute at peak.
[00:52] Marcus Lee: Also need to flag compliance: some customer docs are EU-only, and we need audit logs + KMS for encryption at rest. SOC2 is required.
[01:00] Ava Chen: Great notes — Redwood has hosted regions in EU and US, SOC2, and KMS integrations for Private/Dedicated. For PLG quickstart you can sign up, get free credits, and be making API calls in minutes; Diego can show the flow and time-to-first-token.
[01:15] Samir Patel: Quick question — do you allow self-serve credit redemption for an org account or is it per-user?
[01:20] Ava Chen: We typically provide an org-level credits code for trials; we'll include that link in follow-up.
[01:25] Diego Morales: If you're okay I'll share my screen and walk through the quickstart repo and code snippet — simple curl or SDK, streaming responses and embeddings as well.
[01:32] Samir Patel: Go for it.
[01:35] [Screen share starts]
[01:40] Diego Morales: Here's the quickstart. Step 1: sign up, claim credits. Step 2: install SDK or call REST. Example curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD_KEY' -d '{"model":"rw-lx-7b", "input":"Summarize..."}' — that'll return streaming tokens. Time-to-first-token generally under 200ms for small prompts on hosted depending on region and model.
[02:05] Jenna Ross: Under 200ms is promising. Is that in steady state or burst?
[02:09] Diego Morales: That's steady-state on our low-latency profiles and smaller models; larger models and cold starts can be higher. We offer latency tiers and can route to Dedicated pools to get more predictable p95.
[02:20] Marcus Lee: For the Dedicated path, what's the onboarding and commit? We may need reserved capacity for predictable SLAs.
[02:26] Ava Chen: Dedicated is typically a monthly reserved capacity contract; we can scope throughput and latency targets during POC. Onboarding timeline is usually 2–6 weeks depending on custom networking (VPC) and certs.
[02:39] Samir Patel: Hmm 2–6 weeks is okay but we want to ramp quickly. We like the idea of starting hosted and moving to Dedicated if latency/cost becomes an issue.
[02:47] Ava Chen: That's a common path. Start hosted with free credits for dev, run pilot benchmarks, then evaluate Dedicated if you need isolation or tighter SLOs.
[02:55] Jenna Ross: About cost: we saw cost variance with other providers; do you have guidance on batching and quantization?
[03:01] Diego Morales: Yes — Redwood Optimize gives model and quantization recommendations per workload. For summarization you can use a 4-bit quantized variant to cut token cost with minimal quality loss. We also have automatic prefix caching for repeated document chains.
[03:15] [03:15] Samir Patel: Can you run a small benchmark against our sample dataset? We can share a subset.
[03:20] Diego Morales: Absolutely — if you share a 1–2k prompt sample we can run throughput/latency and token-cost estimates. I'll need sample format (JSONL etc.).
[03:28] Jenna Ross: We can export as JSONL. I'll put together a 500-sample test.
[03:33] Ava Chen: Perfect. We'll also send a quickstart link and credits. Expect an org code that can be redeemed in the Console.
[03:40] Marcus Lee: About security: for Private deployment do you support customer KMS/HSM and air-gapped on-prem?
[03:47] Diego Morales: Yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS with HSM integrations, and we offer an on-prem package for regulated customers. That typically adds to lead time.
[03:57] Samir Patel: Do you provide audit logs and retention controls for hosted?
[04:00] Ava Chen: Hosted includes standard audit logs and retention settings; Enterprise/Private gives more granular retention and export options. We'll attach our SOC2 and security docs after the call.
[04:09] Jenna Ross: Are there any gotchas around VPC peering or egress in Private?
[04:13] Marcus Lee: We need to know allowed ports, any NAT requirements.
[04:16] Diego Morales: For Private we do VPC peering or private link; SE will coordinate with your infra to confirm ports and subnets. For hosted, egress isn't required since calls are outbound to our API.
[04:27] [04:27] Samir Patel: What about data residency? Can we pin to EU region and ensure logs stay in region?
[04:32] Ava Chen: Yes — for hosted we have EU regions and can pin workloads; for compliance we recommend Dedicated or Private so data and logs are fully isolated and region-restricted.
[04:41] Jenna Ross: Onboarding: what's the fastest path to get devs in and testing in our sandbox?
[04:45] Diego Morales: Quickstart: 1) sign up and confirm org, 2) redeem credits, 3) SDK + example repo, 4) run sample requests. Most teams hit first token within 10–20 minutes. We'll include code snippets and a Postman collection.
[04:58] Samir Patel: Nice. Any limits on free credits or rate limits during trial?
[05:03] Ava Chen: There's a trial quota to prevent abuse; we'll share the exact amount in the follow-up. For higher rate testing we can lift limits during a POC.
[05:12] Jenna Ross: Competitors we looked at had issues with streaming stability and missing KV cache — does Redwood support KV cache to speed up long conversations?
[05:20] Diego Morales: Yes, our runtime manages KV cache efficiently and you can commit prefixes to cache for repeated contexts which helps latency and cost.
[05:28] [05:28] Samir Patel: Regarding models, are there Redwood-curated open models available? Any proprietary models?
[05:34] Ava Chen: We host curated open models with verified performance profiles. We also partner with a few vendors but our PLG offering is focused on open and community models; we can discuss larger model options if you need them.
[05:46] Marcus Lee: For networking: if we wanted Private, what are the typical network architecture choices?
[05:51] Diego Morales: We support VPC peering, PrivateLink, or on-prem. SE will share a network checklist.
[05:57] Jenna Ross: SLA questions — does hosted have an SLA?
[06:00] Ava Chen: Hosted has no formal SLA on the free tier; enterprise plans and Dedicated carry SLA commitments. We can share SLA tiers.
[06:08] [06:08] Samir Patel: Timeline-wise, we're aiming to decide vendor in two months. We want a pilot in 3–4 weeks. Is that feasible?
[06:14] Ava Chen: Yes, that's a reasonable timeline: quickstart and credits now, run pilot within 2–4 weeks, then evaluate Dedicated/Private if needed.
[06:20] Diego Morales: I'll follow up with a benchmark plan and what we need from you.
[06:26] [06:26] Jenna Ross: One more technical — how do you handle token accounting across streaming responses and function calls?
[06:32] Diego Morales: The Console shows token-level breakdowns per call including streaming tokens, prompt vs completion. For complex function/tool calling we surface costs per invocation.
[06:41] Samir Patel: Good. Any examples of customers in our space?
[06:45] Ava Chen: We've worked with several SaaS customers doing summarization and search, happy to share anonymized case studies.
[06:52] [06:52] Marcus Lee: Ok, let's talk risk: what would cause us to choose a competitor? Price or latency?
[06:58] Jenna Ross: If we can't meet p95 or costs balloon during scale, that's a dealbreaker.
[07:04] Ava Chen: Understood — we'll prioritize benching those SLOs. Diego will run localized latency tests and cost projections.
[07:12] [07:12] Diego Morales: For the benchmark I'll run p50/p95/p99 for your JSONL sample across rw-lx-7b and rw-lx-3b quantized variants and include cost estimates.
[07:23] Samir Patel: Perfect. How soon can you get that back?
[07:26] Diego Morales: If you share samples by Friday I'll get initial numbers early next week.
[07:31] [07:31] Jenna Ross: We'll aim to share Friday.
[07:34] Ava Chen: Quick recap: send quickstart + credits, SE demo scheduling, share dataset, security docs and pricing. Anything else?
[07:44] Marcus Lee: Please include Private networking checklist and KMS options.
[07:48] Ava Chen: Will do.
[07:50] [Silence / typing]
[08:00] [08:00] Samir Patel: One last thought — do you have any usage-based cost controls to prevent runaway bills in prod?
[08:07] Diego Morales: Yes, Console supports per-key quotas, rate limits, and alerting. We can also help set budget caps during pilot.
[08:15] [08:15] Jenna Ross: Great.
[08:17] Ava Chen: Alright thanks everyone — we'll follow up with links. Diego, any final notes?
[08:21] Diego Morales: I'll send the benchmark plan and ask for the sample format.
[08:25] Ava Chen: Thanks all. We'll send notes and next steps after this.
[08:30] [Call ends — actual transcript continues with small talk and hangups omitted]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "rw-lx" may be transcribed as "our el ex"), filler words retained. References shared: Quickstart repo link: https://redwood.ai/quickstart (link to follow-up), Security packet: https://redwood.ai/security (to be attached).

End of transcript.
